rationale: Across published cohorts characterizing pathogenic variants in MAU2 (such as Parenti et al., describing 18 individuals with 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants), probands present with microcephaly, short stature, and variable CdLS features ranging from mild to classic facial gestalt. However, severe limb reduction defects (such as phocomelia, amelia, or severe transverse limb deficiencies) and diaphragmatic hernia have remained characteristic of classical CdLS1 caused by truncating NIPBL variants and are not standard or prevalent manifestations of MAU2 variants, confirming that their presence points away from MAU2-CdLS7 toward classic NIPBL etiology.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. characterize the definitive clinical cohort of 18 individuals with 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants, demonstrating a range of phenotypes characterized predominantly by short stature, microcephaly, and variable facial and neurodevelopmental traits, without reporting recurrent severe limb reduction deficiencies or structural diaphragmatic defects seen in classical NIPBL-mediated CdLS.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2 lead to a new Cornelia de Lange Syndrome subtype
source.quote: We describe 18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants and demonstrate pathogenicity through functional analyses... Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as consistent features.

evidence.text: Investigation of NIPBL-MAU2 interaction and mutant cohorts indicates that severe classical structural limb anomalies in CdLS are linked to specific NIPBL disruptions rather than general disruption of the loader complex alone.

source.title: Isolated NIBPL missense mutations that cause Cornelia de Lange syndrome alter MAU2 interaction
source.quote: These data suggest that factors in addition to MAU2 are essential in determining the clinical features and severity of CdLS.

evidence.text: Frank limb reduction defects represent a distinct phenotypic entity restricted to specific genetic subsets within CdLS (principally truncating NIPBL mutations), and genetic disruption of cohesin loading mechanisms does not routinely generate limb reductions.

source.title: Genetic enhancement of limb defects in a mouse model of Cornelia de Lange syndrome
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part C: Seminars in Medical Genetics
source.quote: However, frank limb reductions, as are seen in a subset of individuals with CdLS, do not occur, suggesting that additional signaling and/or gene regulatory pathways are involved in producing such dramatic changes.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence of minor digital abnormalities (e.g., fifth finger clinodactyly, small hands) versus severe reduction defects across an expanded worldwide registry of MAU2 probands?
new_directions.rationale: While severe limb reductions have not been observed in initial MAU2 cohorts, quantifying the frequency of milder acral abnormalities will refine distinguishing clinical criteria against non-classic CdLS subtypes.
